Why Klein Curaçao

The best beach in Curaçao isn't on Curaçao.

Klein Curaçao lies 10 km offshore, a flat, uninhabited island where nothing stays except a lighthouse and the sea turtles that return here to nest every year. No shops. No signal. Just one of the longest stretches of white sand in the Caribbean. A full day to disappear. We've been on every boat that makes the trip. We've never met anyone who regretted going.

The crossing sails against the trade winds. Some mornings it's glass-smooth. Others, the catamaran earns its way there. Worth it. All of it.

Discover Klein Curaçao

A 1.7 km² flat, uninhabited island, 10 kilometers off the southeast coast of Curaçao. No shops, no signal, just sand, reef, and history.

The White Beach

A long, wide stretch of white sand on the lee side, facing water so calm it barely counts as sea. The boats anchor right off it. Walk five minutes in either direction and you have a piece of it to yourself.

Photo pendingeditorial.history · archive scan queue

History

In 1871 the British mining engineer John Godden found phosphate here and dug out tens of thousands of tons of it, leaving the island meters lower and stripped bare, which is why it is flat and treeless today. Before that, ships anchored here in quarantine before entering Curaçao. The lighthouse and the wrecks are what the sea added since.

Sea Turtles

Green turtles graze the seagrass beds just off the anchorage. Sightings are common, never guaranteed, and never baited. Keep two meters of distance and they will keep grazing while you float above.

Snorkeling & Diving

The anchorage sits over sand and seagrass in shallow, clear turquoise water: easy, warm, and full of life that does not mind visitors. Masks are free on most boats in limited numbers, fins usually are not, so bring your own if you use them.

The Pink Lighthouse

A faded rose tower from 1913 in the middle of the island, twenty to thirty minutes on foot from the beach with barely any shade on the way. You can walk up to it, and the view over the whole island is worth the sweat. Bring water and go before noon.

Shipwrecks

On the rough windward shore a wreck rusts into the rocks, close enough to walk to from the lighthouse. The surf on that side is serious; look, photograph, and keep your feet on land. It is the most photographed rust in the Caribbean for a reason.

What we tell first-timers about Klein Curaçao

Take water shoes
The open bar opens after arrival
There is no phone signal
Sit at the back
Heading out, you sail straight into the trade winds, so the front of the boat takes the chop. Sit at the back, ideally back-centre, keep your eyes on the horizon, and most queasiness settles before the island shows up.
No need to rush ashore
There are enough beach beds and palapas for everyone, so take your time getting off the boat. The only perk of the first tender is first pick of your spot for the day.
Bring reef-safe sunscreen
Reef-safe only, and more of it than you think. There is almost no natural shade outside the palapas, and ordinary sunscreen harms the reef the whole day floats over.
Barely any phone signal
Signal is weak or absent the whole day. Tell whoever needs to know before you leave the dock, download anything you need offline, then enjoy being unreachable.
Book weeks ahead
The limited-availability line is real here: trips genuinely sell out three to four weeks ahead, year-round. If you know your dates, lock them in early.
Mind the lighthouse stairs
You can climb up for a view over the whole island, but the stairs are weathered and unmaintained. Take them slowly, watch your footing, and hold on.

Frequently asked questions

Is Klein Curaçao worth it?
Yes. Most visitors call it the day that made their Curaçao trip: one of the longest white-sand beaches in the Caribbean, a full day on the sand and in the water, and turtles grazing the shallows. The island is completely undeveloped, the boat carries everything, and that is exactly the appeal.
What is there to do on Klein Curaçao?
Swim, snorkel the seagrass for turtles, walk to the pink lighthouse and the shipwreck, eat from the grill, and do nothing under a palapa. The whole island walks end to end in under an hour; five hours ashore fills itself.
How much does a Klein Curaçao trip cost?
Shared day trips start from $135 per person, including breakfast and a BBQ lunch. The powerboat and the super yachts set their own rates, and private charters are priced per boat.
How long is the boat trip to Klein Curaçao?
45 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes each way, depending on the boat. Most boats run 8 to 9 hours dock to dock (the Powerboat Adventure is a shorter 6-hour day), with about five hours at the island. Departures leave early, usually before 8:30 AM, and are back before dinner.
Will I get seasick on the way to Klein Curaçao?
The way out runs against the trade wind and can be bouncy, especially January through July. Sit at the back, keep your eyes on the horizon, and take seasickness medicine 30 minutes before departure if you are sensitive. The return is usually calmer.
What should I bring to Klein Curaçao?
Reef-safe sunscreen, a towel, a dry bag for your phone, water shoes for the rocky stretches, your own fins if you snorkel seriously, and some cash for the crew. The boats carry food, drinks and limited free masks.
Are there toilets on Klein Curaçao?
Not on the island itself: it is uninhabited, with no shops and no facilities ashore. The boats stay anchored all day and their toilets stay open; the bigger catamarans carry two.
Is Klein Curaçao suitable for families with young children?
Yes, with the right boat. The family motorboat is the steadiest hull and the easiest boarding, and the beach shelves gently on the lee side. The crossing is the only rough part of the day; young children handle it best at the back, midship, in the shade.
What happens if the weather is bad on my Klein Curaçao trip?
Skippers make the call, and safety wins every time. When an operator cancels a sailing you choose between a full refund and a free move to a new date, and every tour can also be cancelled for free by you; the exact cut-off is on the tour page.
